fields.title: Knowledge as code: a structured, validated wiki that AI sessions can read and contribute to

sections.Context: What the consortium knows about its own systems sits in the staff wiki, the work tracker and the platform team's memory, and nothing connects them. Metadata written in prose cannot be validated or indexed, so hand-kept indexes drift. A page listing which services call another is correct the day somebody writes it, and nothing says when it stopped being correct. An AI coding session that cannot find the conventions breaks them with confidence, and what it discovers is lost when the session ends.
sections.Decision:
We treat knowledge as code:

* **Every document has a type and validated frontmatter.** The type comes from a
  [taxonomy](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/874d89634b8ad6af2347002d8e5cb4ce21e243f8/examples/library/knowledge-as-code/taxonomy.md), and the frontmatter follows a
  [schema](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/874d89634b8ad6af2347002d8e5cb4ce21e243f8/examples/library/knowledge-as-code/metadata.md). The type's tier sets its review bar and its lifecycle.
* **Cheap capture happens in the tracker.** A session files an observation as a work item. It becomes a service record
  or a runbook only when a person verifies it.
* **CI validates** the frontmatter, the ids and the links, and generates every index.

[Knowledge as Code](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/874d89634b8ad6af2347002d8e5cb4ce21e243f8/examples/library/knowledge-as-code.md) describes the full approach.
sections.Consequences:
* **Every document will acquire a schema obligation.** A contributor picks a type and completes the frontmatter, which
  adds friction in exchange for validation.
* **CI will gate documentation.** A malformed document fails the build, and the first few failures could irritate.
* **Branch staff will meet a metadata table above every page**, written for automation.
* **Existing wiki content will have to migrate**, and somebody has to decide which pages are worth keeping.
* **The value depends on that verification.** If unverified observations reach the corpus, trust in everything else
  falls with them.
* **Session logs will stay out of this corpus**, because they contain borrower data and credentials.
